en: Jose Rizal was a polymath who could speak 22 different languages, including Latin, Greek, and Japanese.
The Philippine Senate has exactly 24 senators who are elected by the entire country rather than specific districts.
The Philippine tarsier has eyes so large that each eyeball is actually bigger than its entire brain.
The Banaue Rice Terraces, carved by the Ifugao people, would stretch halfway around the globe if laid end to end.
Doctor Fe del Mundo invented a unique bamboo incubator that uses hot water bottles to keep premature babies warm.
The eight rays of the sun on the Philippine flag represent the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish rule.
Before the Spanish arrived, ancient Filipinos wrote their native languages using Baybayin, an alphabet carved into bamboo and leaves.
During the Pahiyas Festival in Lucban, locals decorate their entire houses with vibrant, edible kiping made from ground rice.
The golden South Sea pearl, recognized as the Philippine national gem, is the largest and most valuable pearl variety.
The Philippines is one of the few countries with a Sangguniang Kabataan, a local youth council run entirely by teenagers.
Juan Luna’s masterpiece Spoliarium is massive, measuring exactly 4.22 meters high and 7.64 meters wide.
The Filipino value of bayanihan originated from the literal practice of an entire community carrying a traditional nipa hut together.
